note: Agents with a new mechanism, target or modality that are not yet approved for this disease in the US or EU, selected from peer-reviewed early-phase trials and major meetings. Early response rates often fall with more patients and longer follow-up; meeting data are not peer-reviewed.
scope: Most new drugs for Waldenström macroglobulinemia are tested first after a BTK inhibitor, so this list covers untreated and relapsed disease together. The evidence is thin for several entries, and that is stated in each.

items.why: Degrading BTK, rather than blocking it, can work against the Cys481 and other BTK mutations that cause resistance to covalent and noncovalent BTK inhibitors, the main unmet need after a BTK inhibitor.
items.data: CaDAnCe-101, Waldenström cohort (EHA 2025): 36 patients treated, all after a covalent BTK inhibitor, with a median of 3 previous lines; among 32 evaluable patients, ORR 84.4%, major response 75.0% and very good partial response 31.3%; median time to first response 1.0 month.
items.safety: Neutropenia 39% (grade 3 or higher, 31%), contusion 31%, diarrhea 25%; 2 patients stopped for adverse events.
items.next: No phase 3 trial in Waldenström macroglobulinemia was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov when checked; phase 3 trials are under way in CLL.

items.tgt: Lipid rafts of tumor cell membranes
items.why: A targeted radiotherapy given as four infusions over two cycles, with a mechanism unrelated to BTK or BCL2, tested in patients who have had at least two previous lines.
items.data: CLOVER-WaM (ASH 2024; data cutoff May 31, 2024): 55 patients in the efficacy population; ORR 83.6%, major response 58.2% (primary endpoint), complete or very good partial response 7.3%.
items.safety: Cytopenias were the most common adverse events; one death from an adverse event (bacterial sepsis).
items.next: Phase 3 against rituximab, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone after a BTK inhibitor (DCL-26-001, NCT07766421), registered and not yet recruiting.

items.ev: Phase 1, meeting data (not yet peer-reviewed); figures not verified here
items.why: A next-generation BCL2 inhibitor, more selective and potent than venetoclax in laboratory studies. Venetoclax is active in this disease but has no approval for it.
items.data: The phase 1 trial (BGB-11417-101) reported responses with sonrotoclax alone in relapsed or refractory disease at doses up to 640 mg; response rates could not be verified from a primary source for this page. A phase 2 trial (BGB-11417-203, 114 patients) tests it alone after a BTK inhibitor and with zanubrutinib as a fixed-duration first treatment.
items.next: BGB-11417-203 (NCT05952037), with major response rate as primary endpoint; a French phase 2 trial of zanubrutinib with sonrotoclax in previously treated patients (WAZABI, NCT06547866).
src: Sarosiek S, Br J Haematol 2025 (review of BCL2 inhibition)

items.why: No CAR T-cell therapy is approved for Waldenström macroglobulinemia, and complete responses are rare with every approved drug.
items.data: In heavily pretreated patients with disease refractory to a BTK inhibitor, the rate of complete or very good partial response was 80%; the number of patients is not reported in the abstract.
items.next: The authors call for larger trials (NCT03277729).

items.why: Six doses of a drug approved for large B-cell lymphoma, tested after rituximab and a BTK inhibitor, including in disease with CXCR4 or TP53 alterations.
items.data: Interim analysis (ASH 2024): 7 patients enrolled; the futility rule required more than 2 responses among the first 7. Higher response rates were reported at ASH 2025; those figures were not verified from the abstract for this page.
items.safety: Skin toxicity and asymptomatic GGT elevation, sometimes persistent after treatment; transient cytopenias; no discontinuations for toxicity in the interim analysis.
